title: A power-multiplicative product-topology norm is spectral
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, and $L/K$ a finite field extension. Suppose $N:L\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ is a $K$-algebra norm: $N(z)=0$ exactly at $0$, $N(1)=1$, $N(z+w)\le\max(N(z),N(w))$, $N(zw)\le N(z)N(w)$ and $N(az)=|a|N(z)$. Assume $N(z^m)=N(z)^m$ for all $m\ge1$. Suppose there are a $K$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_d$ of $L$ and constants $c,C>0$ such that $$c\max_i|a_i|\le N(\sum_i a_iw_i)\le C\max_i|a_i|\qquad(a_i\in K).$$ Then $N=s_{L/K}$, the minimal-polynomial spectral norm [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. No completeness, normality or separability of $L/K$ is assumed.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Distinguished presentations of reduced affinoids over an algebraically closed field. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. Supporting analytic lemma in the presentation construction: Norm-preserving lifts for a Tate epimorphism surjective on canonical reductions. Independent analytic input: Finite affinoid maps are finite on spectral unit balls over an algebraically closed field. Proof input: Orthogonal spectral norm on the fraction field of a finite affinoid domain. Supporting input: Stability of the Gauss fraction field of a Tate algebra. BGR stability proof input: Sections 5.3.3–5.3.4, especially Proposition 5.3.3/3 and the conclusion of Section 5.3.4, printed pp.215 and 218–220 (scan PDF pp.221 and 224–226); Section 5.3.4 removes the divisible-value-group restriction. Supporting input for the present split: Lemma 3.5.1/1, printed pp.151–152 (scan PDF pp.159–160), in particular its power-multiplicative case; used at the conclusion of Section 5.3.4, printed p.220.
